mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has fallen in each of the last four weeks (-10.1, -32.0, -36.6, -52.4), indicating strong negative momentum driven by self-reinforcing reductions in discretionary outings; this trend is expected to persist and pull the next-4-week mean lower than the prior-4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC declined monotonically over all four observed weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC mean over the next 28 days is higher than or equal to the last 28-day mean despite the four-week monotonic decline, rejecting pure momentum persistence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained and accelerating rise in RESIDENTIAL mobility (6.7 to 21.0 over four weeks) signals intensifying stay-at-home policy compliance or mandates; once cumulative residential gain exceeds 15 points over three weeks, retail trips are further curtailed as households shift to home-centered routines, depressing RETAIL_REC over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL cumulative increase exceeds 15 points over the trailing three weeks
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL rose from 6.7 to 21.0 over four weeks, a 14.3-point increase
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next two weeks even though RESIDENTIAL cumulative gain exceeded the 15-point threshold, indicating the residential-driven suppression mechanism does not hold.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous sharp declines in TRANSIT (-20.6 to -55.4) and WORKPLACES (-16.0 to -40.6) jointly suppress the pool of people who would otherwise combine commuting with retail errands; the interaction of collapsing transit use and workplace attendance compounds to produce a steeper drop in RETAIL_REC than either series alone would predict, persisting over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES declined in every observed week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC's next-4-week mean does not fall further despite continued joint decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES, indicating no compounding interaction effect between commute-linked series.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening-restrictions regime, the combination of falling PARKS mobility (27.3 to -15.6) and rising RESIDENTIAL mobility signals active lockdown enforcement that curtails both outdoor and errand-based movement; under this specific regime, RETAIL_REC is expected to continue declining over the next two weeks as restrictions bind harder.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell from 27.3 to -15.6 while RESIDENTIAL rose from 6.7 to 21.0
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next two weeks even though PARKS remains negative and RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, indicating the regime-conditional lockdown mechanism is not operative.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS rebound from -19.3 to -2.9 between t-2w and t-1w before falling again suggests weather-driven volatility in outdoor activity; if seasonal conditions continue improving, some outdoor-to-indoor substitution will ease and partially restore short-term retail trips, producing a modest rebound in RETAIL_REC within the next four weeks relative to the recent trough.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS showed a non-monotonic rebound from -19.3 to -2.9 before declining to -15.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next four weeks despite any PARKS rebound, showing no seasonal substitution relief for retail activity.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM has stayed roughly flat to slightly negative (4.4 to -4.4) while RETAIL_REC collapsed (-10.1 to -52.4), indicating a behavioral substitution where households preserve essential shopping but cut discretionary retail; this divergence is expected to persist, keeping RETAIL_REC depressed relative to GROCERY_PHARM over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM remained near baseline while RETAIL_REC fell over 40 points
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC and GROCERY_PHARM move together (converge) over the next four weeks, indicating no essential-versus-discretionary substitution effect.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility decline accelerated week-on-week, with the drop from t-1w to t-0w (-25.6 to -40.6, a 15-point fall) exceeding prior weekly changes; once the week-on-week WORKPLACES drop exceeds 10 points, reduced office-adjacent foot traffic quickly transmits to nearby retail within one week, producing an immediate further decline in RETAIL_REC.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES fell 15.0 points from t-1w to t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall further in the week immediately following a WORKPLACES week-on-week drop exceeding 10 points, rejecting the fast transmission mechanism.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility and RETAIL_REC have moved in close lockstep across all four weeks (both declining steadily), reflecting that transit usage is a direct proxy for people traveling to retail destinations; continued TRANSIT decline is expected to predict continued RETAIL_REC decline within the very next week.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT declined every week from -20.6 to -55.4, paralleling RETAIL_REC's decline
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises in the next week even as TRANSIT continues to decline, indicating the transit-retail co-movement linkage has broken down.
